text:
Matthew Knies hasn't scored in 15 games, his first 16 since moving from Toronto to Columbus, and Sportskeeda has already found fans arguing the fit is wrong. He has 2 goals and 7 points while playing 18 minutes a night.

This isn't pure bad luck. Our numbers call it a real dip: 3 points in his last ten games against about 7 expected at his ice time, and his own chances have dried up too (1.7 expected goals over that stretch against 2.5 usual). Columbus gets 48% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, about the same as without him.

The context from last season matters. Evolving-Hockey had him facing the other team's best (97th percentile competition) and creating little offense with him on (bottom 6% of forwards), so he's never been a pure offensive driver. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking gives him a distinct habit: 18% of his setups come from behind the net, more than double a typical forward, and 56% of his shots come off the rush. Watch whether Columbus plays to those strengths. Right now the chances, not just the goals, are missing.
headline: Matthew Knies is searching in Columbus
